title.narrative: Engaging men and boys as a pre-requisite for effectively addressing violence against women and girls in Eastern Africa

description.narrative: In the 21st century, despite great strides globally towards gender equality in recent decades, gender-based violence, discrimination, and inequalities remain a reality, with spikes in times of crises and wars, as witnessed in Eastern Africa during COVID-19, where cases of GBV have increased drastically. On the frontlines of essential jobs with perilous working conditions and low wages, women are missing at the highest levels of leadership and management. Since 2020, 1 in 2 women reported having experienced or witnessed violence. In addition to treating the symptoms of gender inequalities, this workplan intends to uncover their origins and shed light on whole-of-society solutions advocating gender equality as an equitable situation for all, and strengthening research and partnerships to addressing biased and discriminatory social gender norms embedded in legal systems, interpersonal relationships and behaviors, and that continuously shape harmful models for societies, sustain the cycle of violence and limit the potential of all women, men and individuals of diverse gender identities – although differently based on context, nationality, ethnicity, socio-economic status, religion, age, disability, sexuality, inter alia.
